server: Web research tools for agents: search, read, crawl, extract, and watch web pages, with typed inputs and capped output. No API key needed.

tools.search: Search the web, Wikipedia, Hacker News, or arXiv without an API key. Use it to find pages on a topic. Returns titles, URLs, and snippets.
tools.scrape: Read one web page as clean Markdown, without menus or ads. Use it when you have a URL and need its text. Returns the page title and Markdown.
tools.map: List the URLs on a site from its sitemap and links. Use it to see what pages a site has before you scrape. Returns a list of URLs.
tools.summarize: Pull the key sentences out of a text or a web page, with no model call. Pass text or url. Returns the top sentences.
tools.crawl: Visit a page and the pages it links to, up to a depth and a page limit. Use it to read a small part of a site at once. Returns each page's URL and Markdown.
tools.extract: Pull named parts of a page with CSS selectors. Use it when you need set fields, like a price or a title. Pass fields as name:selector pairs, or one selector. Returns the matched text.
tools.answer: Answer a question from a few web sources, with no model call. Use it for a quick fact with sources. Returns the key sentences and the URLs they came from.
tools.research: Dig into a topic across many web sources. Use it when one search is not enough. Returns key points with their source URLs.
tools.parse: Turn a local file, such as a PDF or an HTML file, into clean text. Use it when the content is on disk, not on the web. Returns the text.
tools.media: Save a page's media to a file: download it, take a screenshot, or print a PDF. Use it when you need the file itself. Returns where the file was saved and its size.
tools.monitor: Check a page for changes since the last check. Use it to watch a page over time. Returns whether it changed and what changed.
tools.batch: Scrape many URLs in one call. Use it when you already have a list of pages. Returns one result per URL, each marked ok or not.
tools.act: Open a page in a real browser and read it, with an optional screenshot. Use it for pages that need JavaScript to show their content. Returns the page text.
tools.feed: Read an RSS or Atom feed. Use it to get the newest posts from a site. Returns each item's title, link, and date.

titles.answer: Answer a question from the web
titles.media: Save page media to a file
titles.act: Open a page in a browser
